family: SI and the CGS electromagnetic family (SI/MKSA, CGS-ESU, CGS-EMU, CGS-Gaussian, Heaviside–Lorentz, and their rationalization/legacy variants)

systems.name: SI (2019 revision)
aliases: ISQ (as the quantity system behind SI)
systems.used_in: Essentially all engineering, metrology, condensed-matter experiment, undergraduate E&M texts (Griffiths, Purcell 3rd ed), most of applied optics and photonics, all NIST/BIPM/CODATA documents, and Jackson 3rd ed. chapters 1–10. Rare in high-energy theory, plasma physics, and astrophysics.

Gauss with a 1/\varepsilon_0 and no 4π: ∇·E = ρ/ε₀
Fine-structure constant written α = e²/(4πε₀ħc)

systems.notes: The identity element of the family: empty generator set, and the target every restoration emits into. For equation-checking only five of the seven base dimensions matter: (M, L, T, Θ, I). Θ enters solely through k_B (thermal/statistical equations only); mol (N) and cd (J) essentially never enter a physics equation being dimension-checked — N is a counting factor that cancels (R = N_A k_B), and cd is photometric. Carry the 5-tuple; keep N and cd as inert slots if full SI coverage is wanted. 2019 redefinition: e, h, k_B, N_A, Δν_Cs, c, K_cd are exact; ε₀ and μ₀ are NO LONGER exact. μ₀ = 4παħ/(e²c), so u_r(μ₀) = u_r(ε₀) = u_r(Z₀) = u_r(α) ≈ 1.5×10⁻¹⁰ (CODATA 2022, 1/α = 137.035999177(21)). μ₀ = 4π×10⁻⁷ N/A² only to ~1.3×10⁻¹⁰ relative. Never changes equation form. Magnetization convention: as written this is the Sommerfeld convention (m = IA, M in A/m, B = μ₀(H+M)); see the separate SI-Kennelly row.
sources: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2007.02473 (From mu_0 to e: impacts of the SI revision on electrical measurement)

systems.notes: Equation-form-identical to SI(2019): empty generator set in both, so a reader can treat them as one system for equations. They differ ONLY in which constants are exact and in numeric values at the 10⁻¹⁰ level. Keep the separate row so a numeric mode picks the right exact/measured status for μ₀, ε₀, e, h, k_B. History: Giorgi proposed the four-unit MKS-with-an-electrical-unit system in Oct 1901; IEC adopted the 'M.K.S. System of Giorgi' in 1935 without fixing the fourth unit; CCE recommended the ampere in 1939; IEC adopted rationalization in 1950 (raising μ₀ by 4π to 4π×10⁻⁷) and affirmed the rationalized value in 1956; CGPM made the ampere a base unit in 1954; 'SI' named 1960.
sources: https://tsapps.nist.gov/publication/get_pdf.cfm?pub_id=926425 (Electromagnetic Units, the Giorgi System, and the Revised SI)

systems.name: Unrationalized MKS (pre-1950 Giorgi; Kennelly-type MKS)
systems.used_in: European electrical-engineering and magnetism literature roughly 1901–1950, before the IEC's 1950 rationalization vote; occasional older Continental magnetism monographs.

per_symbol_rescalings.why: The 1950 IEC rationalization multiplied the vacuum permeability by 4\pi. Before it, the Ampère force law read dF/d\ell = 2\mu_0 I_1I_2/d with \mu_0 = 10^{-7}, numerically the same force as the modern 2(\mu_0/4\pi)I_1I_2/d.
Follows from \varepsilon_0\mu_0 = 1/c^2 once \mu_0 is divided by 4\pi.
Unrationalization: the 4\pi moves out of Coulomb's law and into Gauss's law. Dimensionless, therefore invisible to the generator solve.
Same unrationalization rider on the auxiliary magnetic field.

fingerprints: 'μ₀ = 10⁻⁷' (NOT 4π×10⁻⁷) in an otherwise MKS/SI-looking paper
4π present in Gauss's law AND SI-looking unit names (weber, tesla, ampere) at the same time
Coulomb written F = q₁q₂/(ε r²) with no 4π but with metre-kilogram-second units
Pre-1950 IEC / electrical-engineering literature
Explicit complaint about 'the evil of the 4π' (Giorgi's phrase) in surrounding text

benchmark_equations.coulomb: F = \dfrac{q_1 q_2}{\varepsilon_0^{\rm unrat} r^2}, with \varepsilon_0^{\rm unrat} = 4\pi\varepsilon_0^{\rm SI}
benchmark_equations.einstein_field: N/A: never used in general relativity. The mechanical EFE G_{\mu\nu} = (8\pi G/c^4)T_{\mu\nu} would be unchanged; the EM stress tensor would carry 1/(4\pi\mu_0^{\rm unrat}).
benchmark_equations.schrodinger_or_dirac: N/A: never used in quantum mechanics. Formally the hydrogen potential would read V = -e^2/(\varepsilon_0^{\rm unrat} r).

systems.notes: UNCERTAIN in detail: primary sources on the exact D/H conventions of pre-1950 unrationalized MKS are thin and inconsistent between authors, and different writers put the 4π in slightly different places. What IS well sourced is the headline fact that the 1950 IEC rationalization multiplied μ₀ by 4π (10⁻⁷ → 4π×10⁻⁷); that is the only fingerprint I would let a tool act on automatically. NAMING TRAP: 'Kennelly system' in the historical-units literature means this unrationalized MKS; 'Kennelly convention' in modern magnetism means something entirely different (magnetic polarization J = μ₀M inside ordinary SI). Do not conflate them.

systems.name: SI with the Kennelly (magnetic-polarization) convention
systems.used_in: European (especially German and IEC-standards) magnetism and magnetic-materials literature; permanent-magnet engineering; some ISO/IEC 80000-6 usage. Coexists with the Sommerfeld convention inside SI; both are recognized.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: \mathbf{J}_{\rm Kennelly} = \mu_0 \mathbf{M}_{\rm Sommerfeld}, so B = \mu_0 H + J instead of B = \mu_0(H + M). J is in tesla; M is in A/m.
per_symbol_rescalings.why: Kennelly defines the magnetic moment as m' = \mu_0 I A (unit Wb·m) rather than m = IA (unit A·m²), so magnetization per unit volume comes out in tesla.
Same redefinition at the level of the dipole moment.
Algebraic consequence of J = \mu_0 M.

fingerprints: 'B = μ₀H + J' or 'B = μ₀H + I' rather than 'B = μ₀(H + M)'
A magnetization-like quantity quoted in tesla rather than A/m
'magnetic polarization' as the quantity name, symbol J or I
Magnetic moment quoted in Wb·m rather than A·m²
Torque written τ = m'×H rather than τ = m×B

benchmark_equations.gauss_law: \nabla\cdot\mathbf{D} = \rho_f unchanged; the magnetic constitutive relation becomes \mathbf{B} = \mu_0\mathbf{H} + \mathbf{J}, \mathbf{H} = (\mathbf{B}-\mathbf{J})/\mu_0
benchmark_equations.schrodinger_or_dirac: i\hbar\partial_t\psi = [-\tfrac{\hbar^2}{2m}\nabla^2 - \tfrac{e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r}]\psi — unchanged; only the Zeeman term's moment normalization shifts by \mu_0

systems.notes: Strictly not a different unit system — the generator set is still empty and the units are still SI — but it is a live per-symbol definitional split that silently injects or removes a factor of μ₀ if ignored. It earns a row precisely because per_symbol_rescalings is the right home for it. The Sommerfeld convention (m = IA, H = B/μ₀ − M) is the one SI 'recognizes' and the one assumed in the plain SI row.
sources: https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1973AmJPh..41..221C/abstract (Conventions for Magnetic Quantities in SI, Am. J. Phys. 41, 221)

systems.name: CGS-Gaussian
systems.used_in: Theoretical E&M (Jackson 1st/2nd ed. throughout, 3rd ed. ch. 11–16; Landau–Lifshitz vols. 2 and 8; Panofsky–Phillips), plasma physics (NRL Plasma Formulary), astrophysics and astrophysical MHD, atomic/molecular/optical physics, nuclear physics, and most of the general-relativity literature on charged black holes.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: B_{\rm G} = c\,B_{q}, where B_q is the SI symbol carried through the pure 4\pi\varepsilon_0 = 1 quotient. Directly against SI: B_{\rm G} = \sqrt{4\pi/\mu_0}\;B_{\rm SI} (1 T ≘ 10^4 G).
per_symbol_rescalings.why: THE acid test. Setting 4\pi\varepsilon_0 = 1 alone leaves [E]/[B] = velocity: the quotient gives Faraday as \nabla\times E = -\partial_t B, but Gaussian writes -\tfrac1c\partial_t B. Gaussian additionally REDEFINES B by one factor of c so that E and B share the dimension M^{1/2}L^{-1/2}T^{-1}. In the Jackson / Babel-of-Units four-parameter language this is k_B = c (vs k_B = 1 for SI, ESU, EMU).
A must scale with B since B = \nabla\times A in both systems; this is also what makes (\phi, \mathbf{A}) a 4-vector with homogeneous dimensions in Gaussian.
Carries BOTH riders at once: 1/c from the symmetric B-normalization and 4\pi from unrationalization.
Follows from H = B - 4\pi M with H and B each rescaled; M picks up the 1/c but NOT the 4\pi.
Pure unrationalization rider: \nabla\cdot D = 4\pi\rho rather than \rho, and D = E + 4\pi P rather than \varepsilon_0 E + P. Dimensionless, therefore invisible to the linear dimension solve.

fingerprints: 4\pi in Maxwell AND no 4\pi in Coulomb: \nabla\cdot E = 4\pi\rho together with F = q_1q_2/r^2
Explicit 1/c in Faraday and in the Lorentz force: \nabla\times E = -\tfrac1c\partial_t B and F = q(E + \tfrac{v}{c}\times B)
\alpha = e^2/(\hbar c) = 1/137; hydrogen V = -e^2/r; a_0 = \hbar^2/(me^2); Ry = e^2/(2a_0)
\mu_B = e\hbar/(2m_e c) — the c in the denominator is the giveaway vs SI

systems.notes:
ANSWER TO THE ACID TEST: Gaussian is NOT a pure quotient of SI by 4πε₀ = 1. Setting 4πε₀ = 1 (ε₀ = 1/4π, hence μ₀ = 4π/c²) reproduces Gaussian's Coulomb law and ∇·E = 4πρ exactly, but reproduces CGS-ESU's magnetic sector, not Gaussian's: the quotient gives ∇×E = −∂_t B and ∇×B − c⁻²∂_t E = 4πc⁻²J. Gaussian is that quotient with B → cB (equivalently H → H/c, A → cA, M → M/c), which is exactly what makes [E] = [B] = M^(1/2)L^(−1/2)T^(−1). Dimensional proof: under 4πε₀ = 1 the SI current dimension collapses to I = M^(1/2)L^(3/2)T^(−2); then [E]_SI = MLT⁻³I⁻¹ → M^(1/2)L^(−1/2)T^(−1) but [B]_SI = MT⁻²I⁻¹ → M^(1/2)L^(−3/2), differing by exactly one power of velocity. Independently confirmed by the k_B column of the Babel-of-Units table (k_B = c for Gaussian and HL; k_B = 1 for ESU, EMU, SI) and by the Wikipedia Gaussian-units statement that E and B sharing a dimension 'amounts to a factor of c between how B is defined in the two unit systems'.

FULL SI→GAUSSIAN TABLE (quantity relations; factors are DIMENSIONFUL, so numeric checks must also convert m/kg/s→cm/g/s):
q_G = q_SI/√(4πε₀); ρ_G = ρ_SI/√(4πε₀); J_G = J_SI/√(4πε₀); I_G = I_SI/√(4πε₀); P_G = P_SI/√(4πε₀)
E_G = √(4πε₀) E_SI; φ_G = √(4πε₀) φ_SI
D_G = √(4π/ε₀) D_SI
B_G = √(4π/μ₀) B_SI; A_G = √(4π/μ₀) A_SI
H_G = √(4πμ₀) H_SI
M_G = √(μ₀/4π) M_SI; m_G = √(μ₀/4π) m_SI
σ_G = σ_SI/(4πε₀); C_G = C_SI/(4πε₀); R_G = 4πε₀ R_SI; L_G = 4πε₀ L_SI
Numeric spot-checks I did by hand including the base-unit conversion: 1 T ≘ 10⁴ G; 1 A/m ≘ 10⁻³ G (emu/cm³); 1 C ≘ 2.99792458×10⁹ Fr; 1 V/m ≘ (1/2.99792458)×10⁻⁴ statV/cm.

GAUSSIAN→HEAVISIDE–LORENTZ (pure √4π rationalization, no c, since both share k_B = c):
q_HL = √(4π) q_G, ρ_HL = √(4π) ρ_G, J_HL = √(4π) J_G, P_HL = √(4π) P_G, M_HL = √(4π) M_G
E_HL = E_G/√(4π), B_HL = B_G/√(4π), D_HL = D_G/√(4π), H_HL = H_G/√(4π), A_HL = A_G/√(4π), φ_HL = φ_G/√(4π)

GAUSSIAN vs ESU vs EMU (all powers of c; everything else identical):
q, ρ, J, I, P, D: ESU = Gaussian = c × EMU
E, φ: ESU = Gaussian = EMU/c
B, A: EMU = Gaussian = c × ESU
H, M: EMU = Gaussian = ESU/c
This is exactly why Gaussian's electric units are ESU (statvolt, statcoulomb) and its magnetic units are EMU (gauss, oersted, maxwell).
sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.01951 (Trapero, 'Babel of Units', Table 1: k_e, k_m, k_B, k_F)
https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.09568 (Quincey, converting equations between SI, Heaviside-Lorentz and Gaussian)
J. D. Jackson, Classical Electrodynamics 3rd ed., Appendix (Tables 3 and 4)

systems.name: CGS-ESU (electrostatic units)
systems.used_in: 19th- and early-20th-century electrostatics, electrochemistry, gas-discharge and ion-mobility work; source of surviving unit names (statvolt, statfarad, 'esu of charge'); appears in older Continental texts and in tables of capacitance quoted in centimetres.

per_symbol_rescalings.why: Unrationalization only. Dimensionless 4\pi, invisible to the dimension solve, so it must be a rider.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: H_{\rm ESU} = 4\pi\,H_q = c^2\mathbf{B}_{\rm ESU} - 4\pi\mathbf{M}_{\rm ESU}, so \nabla\times\mathbf{H} = 4\pi\mathbf{J} + \partial_t\mathbf{D}
per_symbol_rescalings.why: Same unrationalization rider. NOTE the vacuum relation is H = c^2 B, because \mu_{\rm vac} = 1/c^2 in ESU.

fingerprints: Coulomb WITHOUT 4\pi: F = q_1q_2/r^2 (same as Gaussian) BUT Faraday and Lorentz WITHOUT 1/c: \nabla\times E = -\partial_t B, F = q(E + v\times B)
Explicit c^{-2} in Ampère–Maxwell: \nabla\times\mathbf{B} - c^{-2}\partial_t\mathbf{E} = 4\pi c^{-2}\mathbf{J}
Statement '\varepsilon_{\rm vac} = 1, \mu_{\rm vac} = 1/c^2'
Capacitance quoted in centimetres ('the capacitance of an isolated sphere equals its radius in cm')
Unit names: statcoulomb / franklin (Fr) / 'esu', statvolt, statampere, statohm, statfarad, stathenry; magnetic ESU units are unnamed and quoted as bare g^{1/2}cm^{-3/2}
B quoted in a unit equal to c_cgs gauss ≈ 3×10^{10} G — an absurdly large number is the tell

benchmark_equations.coulomb: F = \dfrac{q_1 q_2}{r^2}\,\hat r — identical to Gaussian
benchmark_equations.einstein_field:
N/A: ESU admits no dimensionally homogeneous F^{\mu
u} (E and B differ by a factor of velocity), so the covariant EM stress tensor cannot be written cleanly and ESU is never used in GR. The mechanical EFE G_{\mu
u} + \Lambda g_{\mu
u} = (8\pi G/c^4)T_{\mu
u} is unaffected.
benchmark_equations.schrodinger_or_dirac: i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi = \left[-\dfrac{\hbar^2}{2m}\nabla^2 - \dfrac{e^2}{r}\right]\psi — IDENTICAL to Gaussian, because q, E and \phi are the same in ESU and Gaussian. The discriminator is the minimal coupling: \left[\gamma^\mu(i\hbar\partial_\mu - qA_\mu) - mc\right]\psi = 0 with NO 1/c, since A_{\rm ESU} = A_{\rm G}/c.

systems.notes: ESU is what makes the acid test sharp: ESU and Gaussian share EXACTLY the same generator (4πε₀ = 1), the same Coulomb law, the same ∇·E = 4πρ, and the same q, ρ, J, E, φ, D, P — yet they are different systems, differing only by B→cB, A→cA, H→H/c, M→M/c. A generator table alone therefore CANNOT distinguish CGS-ESU from CGS-Gaussian. This is the strongest argument in the family for keeping per_symbol_rescalings as a first-class field. ESU is the pure 4πε₀ = 1 quotient of SI in its microscopic sector (E, B, q, ρ, J, A, φ); the only riders are the 4π on D and H from unrationalization. Verified against the CGS Wikipedia article's ESU Maxwell equations (∇·E = 4πρ, ∇×B − c⁻²Ė = 4πc⁻²J), which match substituting ε₀ = 1/4π, μ₀ = 4π/c² into SI term by term. Unit check: the ESU unit of B is g^(1/2)cm^(−3/2) = c_cgs gauss = 2.99792458×10¹⁰ G, confirming B_G = c·B_ESU.
sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.01951 (Table 1: esu has k_e = 1, k_m = c^-2, k_B = 1, k_F = 1)

systems.name: CGS-EMU (electromagnetic units)
systems.used_in: Classical magnetism and magnetometry; source of gauss, oersted, maxwell, gilbert; still pervasive in experimental magnetic-materials literature (VSM/SQUID output quoted in 'emu'); 19th-century telegraphy and the ancestor of the practical volt/ohm/ampere.

per_symbol_rescalings.why: Unrationalization rider; note \varepsilon_{\rm vac} = 1/c^2 in EMU.
Unrationalization rider; \mu_{\rm vac} = 1 makes H numerically equal to B in vacuum, which is why 1 Oe and 1 G are interchangeable in free space.

fingerprints: Coulomb WITH an explicit c^2: F = c^2 q_1q_2/r^2 — the single most diagnostic equation in the family
\nabla\cdot\mathbf{E} = 4\pi c^2\rho; \nabla\times\mathbf{B} - c^{-2}\partial_t\mathbf{E} = 4\pi\mathbf{J}
Biot–Savart with no constant at all: \mathbf{B} = \oint I\,d\boldsymbol\ell\times\hat r/r^2; Ampère force dF/d\ell = 2I_1I_2/d
Statement '\mu_{\rm vac} = 1, \varepsilon_{\rm vac} = 1/c^2'
Unit names: abampere / biot (Bi), abvolt, abcoulomb, abohm, abfarad, abhenry; gauss, oersted, maxwell, gilbert
Inductance quoted in centimetres
Magnetometry usage: moment in 'emu' (= erg/G = G·cm^3 = 10^{-3} A·m^2), magnetization in 'emu/cm^3', mass magnetization in 'emu/g'

benchmark_equations.einstein_field:
N/A: like ESU, EMU has no dimensionally homogeneous F^{\mu
u} ([E]/[B] is a velocity), so it is never used in GR. Mechanical EFE unaffected: G_{\mu
u} + \Lambda g_{\mu
u} = (8\pi G/c^4)T_{\mu
u}.
benchmark_equations.schrodinger_or_dirac: N/A in practice: EMU is never used for atomic quantum mechanics. Formally the hydrogen Hamiltonian would read i\hbar\partial_t\psi = [-\tfrac{\hbar^2}{2m}\nabla^2 - c^2e^2/r]\psi and the fine-structure constant would be \alpha = c\,e_{\rm EMU}^2/\hbar — a strong argument for why nobody does this.

systems.notes: EMU is the pure μ₀/(4π) = 1 quotient of SI in its microscopic sector — verified by substituting μ₀ = 4π and ε₀ = 1/(4πc²) into the SI Maxwell equations and recovering the Wikipedia EMU forms term by term (∇·E = 4πc²ρ, ∇×B − c⁻²Ė = 4πJ). Like ESU, k_B = 1: EMU does NOT rescale B. Consequences worth encoding: B_EMU = B_Gaussian exactly (hence gauss is the B unit of both), H_EMU = H_Gaussian exactly (oersted), M_EMU = M_Gaussian, A_EMU = A_Gaussian; but q_G = c·q_EMU and E_G = E_EMU/c. Unit relations: 1 abC = c_cgs statC = 2.99792458×10¹⁰ Fr; 1 statvolt = c_cgs abvolt; 1 abA = 10 A; 1 abV = 10⁻⁸ V. TRAP: in materials science 'emu' is written as if it were a unit of magnetic moment (1 emu = 1 erg/G = 1 G·cm³ = 10⁻³ A·m²) and 'emu/cm³' as a unit of magnetization; e-magnetica and NIST both flag this as an abuse — emu is a SYSTEM, not a unit. A parser should accept it but tag it. Also: χ_SI = 4πχ_cgs, μ_r = 1 + χ_SI vs μ = 1 + 4πχ_cgs, and demagnetizing factors sum to 1 in SI but 4π in cgs.
sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.01951 (Table 1: emu has k_e = c^2, k_m = 1, k_B = 1, k_F = 1)

systems.name: Heaviside–Lorentz
aliases: natural units (in particle-physics papers, when combined with ħ=c=1)
systems.used_in: Quantum field theory and particle physics (Peskin–Schroeder, Weinberg QFT, Srednicki), lattice gauge theory, most of the QED literature, and increasingly in relativistic plasma / astro-particle work. Also Weinberg's Gravitation and Cosmology.

per_symbol_rescalings.relation: B_{\rm HL} = c\,B_q, where B_q is the SI symbol under the pure \varepsilon_0 = 1 quotient. Directly against SI: B_{\rm HL} = B_{\rm SI}/\sqrt{\mu_0} = c\sqrt{\varepsilon_0}\,B_{\rm SI}.

Scales with B, since B = \nabla\times A.

family_notes:
ACID TEST — THE ANSWER. Gaussian units are NOT a pure quotient of SI by 4πε₀ = 1. They are that quotient PLUS a definitional rescaling of B by one factor of c (and correspondingly A by c, H by 1/c, M by 1/c). schema_fit for Gaussian is needs_symbol_rescaling, and the same holds for Heaviside–Lorentz.

The derivation, done independently and then cross-checked: setting 4πε₀ = 1 forces ε₀ = 1/4π and hence μ₀ = 1/(ε₀c²) = 4π/c². Substituting those into the SI Maxwell equations term by term gives ∇·E = 4πρ, ∇×E = −∂B/∂t, and ∇×B − c⁻²∂E/∂t = 4πc⁻²J. The first is Gaussian's; the second and third are NOT — they are exactly CGS-ESU's. Gaussian is that same ESU set under B → cB. The dimension algebra says the same thing: 4πε₀ = 1 collapses the SI current dimension to I = M^(1/2)L^(3/2)T^(−2), whereupon [E]_SI = M L T^(−3) I^(−1) → M^(1/2)L^(−1/2)T^(−1) while [B]_SI = M T^(−2) I^(−1) → M^(1/2)L^(−3/2). Those differ by exactly one power of velocity, so the quotient alone can never deliver Gaussian's defining property [E] = [B]. Independent confirmation: the four-parameter table in Trapero's "Babel of Units" lists k_B = c for Gaussian and Heaviside–Lorentz and k_B = 1 for SI, ESU and EMU; and Wikipedia's Gaussian-units article states that E and B sharing a dimension "amounts to a factor of c between how B is defined in the two unit systems."

CLEAN STRUCTURAL RESULT — A 2×2 CLASSIFICATION. Two independent riders sit on top of a single generator choice and generate the whole family:
  (i) the c-rider ("symmetric/relativistic B"): B → cB, A → cA, H → H/c, M → M/c. Present in Gaussian and Heaviside–Lorentz; absent in SI, ESU, EMU.
  (ii) the 4π-rider ("unrationalized"): D → 4πD, H → 4πH, so D = E + 4πP, H = B − 4πM, and the 4π moves out of Coulomb into Gauss. Present in Gaussian, ESU, EMU and unrationalized MKS; absent in SI and Heaviside–Lorentz.
So SI = (no, no); Heaviside–Lorentz = (yes, no); ESU/EMU = (no, yes); Gaussian = (yes, yes). Note M picks up the c-rider but NOT the 4π-rider, while H picks up both — I verified this from H = B − 4πM in each system. Both riders are invisible to the linear dimension solve (4π is dimensionless; c is a dimension that ε₀ or μ₀ alone cannot supply), which is exactly why numeric_factor and per-symbol riders must be stored separately from the generator table.

WHAT THIS BREAKS IN A GENERATOR-ONLY SCHEMA. CGS-ESU and CGS-Gaussian have the IDENTICAL generator (4πε₀ = 1, numeric factor 4π), the identical Coulomb law F = q₁q₂/r², the identical ∇·E = 4πρ, and identical q, ρ, J, E, φ, D, P — yet they are different systems. A generator table alone provably cannot tell them apart. Concretely: if a tool tries to convert Gaussian's Faraday law to SI by inserting powers of (4πε₀), the linear system is INCONSISTENT — no power of a constant with dimension (−1,−3,4,0,2) yields a pure velocity — and the solver fails. That failure is itself a useful signal: an unsolvable restoration in this family almost always means "this system carries a hidden factor of c on B." An implementation can either (a) store the riders explicitly, or (b) admit c into the restoration basis for systems flagged k_B = c. The two are equivalent for this family, but (a) is safer, because (b) destroys uniqueness in equations where c legitimately appears on its own.

ESU / EMU / GAUSSIAN TRIANGLE (all factors are powers of c; everything else is identical):
  q, ρ, J, I, P, D:  ESU = Gaussian = c × EMU
  E, φ:              ESU = Gaussian = EMU / c
  B, A:              EMU = Gaussian = c × ESU
  H, M:              EMU = Gaussian = ESU / c
This is the precise sense in which "Gaussian takes its electric quantities from ESU and its magnetic quantities from EMU," and it is why Gaussian's units are statvolt/statcoulomb (ESU) on the electric side and gauss/oersted/maxwell (EMU) on the magnetic side. Unit checks: 1 abC = c_cgs statC = 2.99792458×10¹⁰ Fr; 1 statvolt = c_cgs abvolt; 1 abA = 10 A; the ESU unit of B is g^(1/2)cm^(−3/2) = c_cgs gauss ≈ 3×10¹⁰ G (verified against the CGS Wikipedia article, which independently gives the ESU B unit as "c_cgs gauss").

WHERE THE 4π SITS (rationalization), at a glance:
  SI:                Coulomb 1/(4πε₀); Gauss ∇·D = ρ;     Ampère ∇×H = J + Ḋ
  Heaviside–Lorentz: Coulomb 1/(4π);   Gauss ∇·D = ρ;     Ampère ∇×H = (1/c)(J + Ḋ)
  Gaussian:          Coulomb 1;        Gauss ∇·D = 4πρ;   Ampère ∇×H = (4π/c)J + (1/c)Ḋ
  ESU:               Coulomb 1;        Gauss ∇·D = 4πρ;   Ampère ∇×H = 4πJ + Ḋ
  EMU:               Coulomb c²;       Gauss ∇·D = 4πρ;   Ampère ∇×H = 4πJ + Ḋ
Rationalized systems (SI, HL) keep 4π out of Maxwell and put it in Coulomb; unrationalized systems (Gaussian, ESU, EMU) do the reverse. EMU's Coulomb law with an explicit c² is the single most diagnostic equation in the family.

DOWNSTREAM 4π TRAPS THAT COST REAL PAPERS. Susceptibility χ_SI = 4π χ_cgs, with μ_r = 1 + χ_SI versus μ = 1 + 4πχ_cgs. Demagnetizing factors: ΣN = 1 in SI but ΣN = 4π in cgs. Maxwell Lagrangian: −(1/4μ₀)F² (SI), −(1/16π)F² (Gaussian), −(1/4)F² (HL). EM stress tensor: (1/μ₀)(…), (1/4π)(…), or no prefactor at all. Reissner–Nordström with G = c = 1: Q²/r² (Gaussian-geometrized) versus Q²/(4πr²) (HL-geometrized). Fine-structure constant: α = e²/(4πε₀ħc) (SI), e²/(ħc) (Gaussian), e²/(4πħc) (HL) — with the natural-units corollary e ≈ 0.303 in HL versus e ≈ 0.0854 in Gaussian. Bohr magneton: eħ/(2m_e) (SI) versus eħ/(2m_e c) (Gaussian).

PER-DOCUMENT VERSUS PER-EQUATION TAGGING. Jackson 3rd ed. is SI for chapters 1–10 and Gaussian for 11–16 (the 1st and 2nd editions are Gaussian throughout). A units engine that assumes one system per document will be wrong about the most-cited E&M textbook in the field. Support per-section, ideally per-equation, system assignment.

SI BASE-DIMENSION ADVICE. For equation checking, carry (M, L, T, Θ, I). Θ appears only via k_B and only in thermal/statistical equations. mol and cd essentially never matter: N cancels between N_A and k_B (R = N_A k_B) and is a counting factor; cd is photometric. Keep them as inert slots if full SI coverage is wanted, but do not let them enter the restoration solve. Half-integer exponents are mandatory here: Gaussian charge is M^(1/2)L^(3/2)T^(−1), and the SI↔Gaussian conversion factors are themselves square roots — √(4πε₀), √(4π/μ₀), √(4πμ₀), √(μ₀/4π).

IMPLEMENTATION WARNING ON NUMERICS. Those conversion factors are DIMENSIONFUL, so a numeric check must also apply the m/kg/s → cm/g/s base conversion. I verified two cases by hand this way: B_G = √(4π/μ₀) B_SI gives 1 T = 10⁴ G, and M_G = √(μ₀/4π) M_SI gives 1 A/m = 10⁻³ emu/cm³ — both correct, and both would come out wrong by factors of ~3.16 if the mechanical base conversion were skipped. This is a good regression test for the engine.

2019 SI. ε₀ and μ₀ are no longer exact: μ₀ = 4πα ħ/(e²c), so u_r(μ₀) = u_r(ε₀) = u_r(Z₀) = u_r(α) ≈ 1.5×10⁻¹⁰ (CODATA 2022). μ₀ equals 4π×10⁻⁷ N/A² only to about 1.3 parts in 10¹⁰. This never changes an equation's form, but a numeric mode must know which constants are exact in which era.

GENUINE UNCERTAINTIES, FLAGGED RATHER THAN GUESSED. (1) The exact D/H conventions of pre-1950 unrationalized MKS: the headline fact that the 1950 IEC rationalization multiplied μ₀ by 4π (10⁻⁷ → 4π×10⁻⁷) is well sourced, but the auxiliary-field conventions vary between authors, and I would not let a tool auto-translate that system. (2) "Variant-Gaussian": one secondary source only (Trapero), no identified textbooks; detect-and-warn, never translate. (3) The QES eleventhgram value is from that same secondary source, not independently verified. (4) The 1.00049 / 0.99985 international-unit ratios are the standard CIPM 1946 figures; my searches confirmed the ampere ratio (1.00015 ≈ 1/0.99985) from BIPM but not the ohm figure directly. NAMING COLLISION to guard against in the data model: "Kennelly system" (historical unrationalized MKS with μ₀ = 10⁻⁷) and "Kennelly convention" (magnetic polarization J = μ₀M inside ordinary SI, versus the Sommerfeld convention with M in A/m) are entirely different things sharing a name.
